claim_verdicts.evidence: Design judgement from outline item 4, stated with its condition ('when its model fits yours'). The factual part, that files spelling the names must follow a rename, is covered by claims 8-11.

Factual part: Keycloak importExport 'If a realm already exists in the server, the import operation is skipped.' The claim is conditional ('while the team changes the realm only via its file'); sec 4 keeps that condition, sec 6 drops it (see issue).

issues.text: Unlisted claim: the clause asserts how AddJwtBearer treats a request that carries no token (it 'reports no caller at all'). Claim 9 covers TestAuthHandler only. No permitted source opened (refs/aspnetcore-docs security/, API reference for AuthenticateResult.NoResult) states JwtBearer's result for a tokenless request.
issues.quote: with no `X-Test-Subject` header it reports no caller at all, like a request without a token
issues.fix: Either end the clause at 'it reports no caller at all' (drop ', like a request without a token'), or keep it and add a ledger claim (kind behavior, version_key aspnetcore): 'JwtBearer returns no result when the request has no bearer token, so the caller is anonymous', with a source_hint to the ASP.NET Core JWT bearer docs.

issues.text: Sec 6 states a team practice as an unconditional fact, while sec 4 and claim 13 carry it as a condition. Nothing in the repository enforces it: Keycloak runs start-dev with its admin console, and the realm file is skipped on import once the realm exists, so the realm can change outside any pull request.
issues.quote: and the team changes the realm only through that file, so a rename arrives in a pull request beside the code it breaks
issues.fix: Replace with the conditional form used in sec 4: 'and as long as the team changes the realm only through that file, a rename arrives in a pull request beside the code it breaks.'

issues.text: nameType/roleType are parameters of System.Security.Claims.ClaimsIdentity (.NET), not an ASP.NET Core setting; the ctor doc says 'The claim type to use for name claims' / 'for role claims'. Saying they 'tell ASP.NET Core' misattributes where the setting lives.
issues.quote: which tell ASP.NET Core which claim holds the caller's name and which holds roles
issues.fix: Change to: 'which tell the identity which claim holds the caller's name and which holds roles'.

issues.text: Claim 11 (six files at stage-2) could not be confirmed by running the Try-it command; only an indirect file-by-file check was possible. The expected result in sec 7 and the suggested answer depend on it.
issues.quote: Expected result: six files, each prefixed with `stage-2:`, four in `DonHang.Api` and two in `DonHang.Tests`
issues.fix: No text change if correct. Before approval, run `git -C examples/don-hang grep -l -E '"(sub|roles|staff)"' stage-2 -- '*.cs'` and paste the output into claim 11's source_hint; change the counts in sec 7 only if the output differs.

issues.text: Claims 1-2 (definition of conformist; attribution to Evans) are unverified: content/versions.yaml has no DDD source and refs/ has no DDD mirror. Not number/syntax, so not blocking.
issues.quote: a downstream context that uses the upstream context's model as it is, with no translation of its own
issues.fix: No lesson text change. Owner: add a DDD reference under `standards` in content/versions.yaml (e.g. Evans' DDD Reference) so claims 1-2 can be checked.

issues.text: 'claim' is not in what I know. The prereq summaries use it ('the access token's `roles` claim') without saying what it is, and Core concepts defines 'claim type' as 'the name a claim goes by', which assumes I already know 'claim'. I guess it is one named entry inside a JWT, but I am guessing, and every section leans on it.
issues.quote: claim type — the name a claim goes by inside ASP.NET Core once a token has been read, which need not be the name written in the token.
issues.fix: Open the 'claim type' line with half a sentence saying what a claim is, e.g. 'a claim is one name–value entry a token carries, such as `sub` or `roles`; its claim type is the name…'.

issues.text: I am told that with renaming left on, `sub` would get 'a longer claim type', but not what would go wrong then. I cannot connect this to conforming: is the problem that `FindFirstValue("sub")` would find nothing, or only that the name looks different? This line is the first of the 'three lines' the section says carry the decision.
issues.quote: Left on, it would give some well-known names, `sub` among them, longer claim types of its own.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after it saying what that would break, e.g. that `FindFirstValue("sub")` would then find no claim, so the API would have to spell a framework name instead of Keycloak's.

issues.text: The section promises 'three lines' but never says which three. The excerpt has about five lines of code plus comments, and the prose walks them without counting. I assume MapInboundClaims, RoleClaimType and RequireRole, but had to work it out.
issues.quote: The production side of the decision is three lines in `Program.cs`.
issues.fix: Name them in that sentence: 'three lines in `Program.cs`: `MapInboundClaims = false`, `RoleClaimType = "roles"` and `RequireRole("staff")`.'

issues.text: The paragraph after the Program.cs excerpt covers the AddJwtBearer options, the renaming default, RoleClaimType, RequireRole, which lines belong to earlier lessons, OrderOwnerHandler outside the excerpt, and two controllers. I had to re-read it twice to separate what is in the block from what is not.
issues.quote: Outside the excerpt, `OrderOwnerHandler` repeats the pattern with `IsInRole("staff")`, which lets staff through to any order, and `FindFirstValue("sub")`, and both orders controllers
issues.fix: Split the paragraph before 'Outside the excerpt', so the second paragraph is only about code not shown in the block.

issues.text: The second misconception repeats almost word for word the realm-file sentence from section 4 ('live in … `keycloak/donhang-realm.json`, which Keycloak imports when it first starts … a rename arrives in a pull request beside the code it breaks'). Reading it a second time made me check whether something new was being said.
issues.quote: The realm's settings live in the same repository, in `keycloak/donhang-realm.json`, which Keycloak imports when it first starts, and the team changes the realm only through that file
issues.fix: Shorten the repeat to a back-reference, e.g. 'and, as section 4 showed, a realm rename arrives in a pull request beside the code it breaks.'

issues.text: The suggested answer lists `Integration/OrdersApiTests.cs`, a file the lesson never mentions. The lesson only told me about `TestAuthHandler` on the test side, so I would not know why a second test file spells Keycloak's names.
issues.fix: Add a short clause in the suggested answer saying what `OrdersApiTests.cs` contains, e.g. that its tests send `X-Test-Roles: staff`, so they spell the realm's role too.

issues.text: Summary line 5 says Keycloak's words stay in `DonHang.Api`, but the lesson and Try it showed they also appear in two `DonHang.Tests` files. The section-4 point was only that they stay out of `DonHang.Domain`; line 5 reads as if it is wider.
issues.quote: Keycloak's words stay in `DonHang.Api`: no class in `DonHang.Domain` reads a token.
issues.fix: Reword to: 'Keycloak's words stay out of `DonHang.Domain`: only `DonHang.Api` and its tests spell them, and no class in the domain reads a token.'

issues.text: q2: the correct option (c) is close to a verbatim join of two lesson sentences ('passes it only the value of `sub`' and 'authentication stays in `DonHang.Api`'), so I can pick it by matching wording.
issues.quote: False, because `OrderOwnerHandler` passes only the value of `sub`, and authentication stays in `DonHang.Api`.
issues.fix: Reword option c to state the consequence, e.g. 'False: the domain's customer lookup receives a plain string, and the token never leaves the API project.'
